note: Small, rustic Alberta Parks campground on the Oldman River floodplain just west of Hwy 2 at Fort Macleod, with shady treed sites and more open ones. The hand pump's water is not safe to drink or use; Fort Macleod has a public dump and potable water station at 215 Mill Street. --Claude
summary: Alberta Parks page (Aug 7, 2026) + shop: C$22 confirmed, 25 sites (15 reservable + 10 FCFS), season May 14 - Oct 1 (was approximate May 15 - Sep 30), max 56 ft, pull_through cleared, dump false; phone 403-394-0150 found; riverfront looks too high - recommend riverview.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored riverfront - recommend riverview): the shop tags all 25 sites 'Near Water - no'. On imagery the campground is a gravel loop round a cottonwood island west of the Hwy 2 bridge. The main Oldman channel is ~100-130 m north of the loop across an open gravel bar with willow scrub. The nearest water is a side braid of the river only ~10-15 m wide that runs along the north end of the loop, ~10-20 m from the loop road behind a thin shrub line; the RVs on imagery sit on the east side of the loop ~80 m from that braid. The campground's own loop road lies between any site and the water, so on-water is ruled out; the main channel is open across the bar from the north end, so a view holds: riverview.
